source.text: שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹתאֵ֭לֶיךָ נָשָׂ֣אתִי אֶת־עֵינַ֑י הַ֝יֹּשְׁבִ֗י בַּשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: The song of the ascents. To you I have lifted up my eyes, the [one] sitting in the heavens.

en.L: A song of ascents. To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I lift up my eyes, [the one] sitting in the heavens.
en.B: A song of ascents. I raise my eyes to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the one who reigns in heaven.
en.R: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. I look up to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You sit on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} throne in heaven.

fr.L: Cantique des montées. Vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} je lève mes yeux, [{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui] sièges dans les cieux.
fr.B: Cantique des montées. Je lève les yeux vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, qui règnes dans les cieux.
fr.R: Chant pour la montée vers Jérusalem. Je lève les yeux vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Tu es assis sur {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} trône dans le ciel.

decisions.reason: As in 120:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1, so the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
decisions.reason: As in 120:1: one of the fifteen songs probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.
The verb (yashav) used of God means sitting as king on his throne (2:4; 29:10).

decisions.choice: I have lifted up: I lift up now
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form often used for past events, but here it describes what the psalmist is doing now.

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem

decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what God's sitting means (m3).

source.text: הִנֵּ֨ה כְעֵינֵ֪י עֲבָדִ֡ים אֶל־יַ֤ד אֲֽדוֹנֵיהֶ֗ם כְּעֵינֵ֣י שִׁפְחָה֮ אֶל־יַ֪ד גְּבִ֫רְתָּ֥הּ כֵּ֣ן עֵ֭ינֵינוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ עַ֝֗ד שֶׁיְּחָנֵּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, as [the] eyes of slaves to [the] hand of their masters, as [the] eyes of a female slave to [the] hand of her mistress, so our eyes [are] to YHWH our God until that he shows us favor.

en.L: Look, as the eyes of slaves [are] to the hand of their masters, as the eyes of a female slave [are] to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes [are] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows us favor.
en.B: Servants watch the hand of their master, and a servant woman watches the hand of the woman she serves. In the same way we keep our eyes on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, waiting for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to show us favor.
en.R: Servants keep watching their master's hand to see what he wants or what he will give. A servant woman watches the hand of the woman she works for. In the same way, we keep looking to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. We wait for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be kind to us.

fr.L: Voici, comme les yeux des esclaves [sont] vers la main de leurs maîtres, comme les yeux d’une esclave [sont] vers la main de sa maîtresse, ainsi nos yeux [sont] vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu, jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous fasse grâce.
fr.B: Les serviteurs regardent la main de leur maître, et la servante regarde la main de sa maîtresse. De même, nous gardons les yeux fixés sur {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu, en attendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous fasse grâce.
fr.R: Les serviteurs regardent sans cesse la main de leur maître pour voir ce qu’il veut ou ce qu’il va leur donner. La servante regarde la main de la femme pour qui elle travaille. De même, nous ne quittons pas des yeux {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu. Nous attendons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit bon pour nous.

decisions.choice: the hand of their master: signal and gift
decisions.reason: Slaves watched the master's hand for a sign of what was wanted, for the food and wages it handed out, and for help. The picture is of complete attention and dependence.
The verb (chanan) means to show undeserved kindness to someone in need. It is repeated twice in verse 3.

decisions.choice: masters: plural of majesty or each one's master
decisions.reason: The word for "their master" is plural in form, as it often is for a master or lord; it may also mean each slave's own master.

decisions.choice: to see what he wants or what he will give
decisions.reason: Readable explains why the servants watch the hand (m1).
"Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that these are slaves watching a master, and Literal keeps "slaves" and "female slave".

decisions.choice: "esclaves", "une esclave" (Literal); "serviteurs", "la servante" (Balanced, Readable) for ʿavadim and shifḥah
decisions.reason: As the French terms set for ʿeved: "esclave" at Literal, "serviteur" at Balanced and Readable, as the English does. The feminine shifḥah follows the same pattern.

source.text: חָנֵּ֣נוּ יְהוָ֣ה חָנֵּ֑נוּ כִּֽי־רַ֝֗ב שָׂבַ֥עְנוּ בֽוּז׃

records.literal_gloss: Show us favor, YHWH, show us favor, for much we have been filled [with] contempt.

en.L: Show us favor, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show us favor, for we have been greatly filled [with] contempt.
en.B: Show us favor, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show us favor, for we have swallowed more contempt than we can bear.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, be kind to us! Be kind to us! People have looked down on us more than we can stand.

fr.L: Fais-nous grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, fais-nous grâce, car nous avons été grandement rassasiés de mépris.
fr.B: Fais-nous grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, fais-nous grâce, car nous avons avalé plus de mépris que nous n’en pouvons supporter.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, sois bon pour nous ! Sois bon pour nous ! Les gens nous ont méprisés plus que nous ne pouvons le supporter.

decisions.choice: filled with contempt: had too much of it
decisions.reason: To be "filled" or "sated" with something is to have had more than enough of it. Here the people have been made to swallow contempt until they can take no more.
The word (buz) is scorn shown to people treated as worthless (Nehemiah 3:36 has the same complaint).

decisions.choice: People have looked down on us
decisions.reason: Readable says who showed contempt and what it was.

source.text: רַבַּת֮ שָֽׂבְעָה־לָּ֪הּ נַ֫פְשֵׁ֥נוּ הַלַּ֥עַג הַשַּׁאֲנַנִּ֑ים הַ֝בּ֗וּז לִגְאֵ֥יוֹנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Much has it been filled for itself, our soul, [with] the mockery of the ones at ease, the contempt of the proud.

en.L: Our soul has been greatly filled for itself [with] the mockery of those at ease, the contempt of the proud.
en.B: We have had our fill and more of the mockery of the comfortable and the contempt of the arrogant.
en.R: We are tired of being mocked by people with easy lives, and of being looked down on by proud people.

fr.L: Notre âme a été grandement rassasiée pour elle-même de la moquerie de ceux qui sont tranquilles, du mépris des orgueilleux.
fr.B: Nous en avons plus qu’assez de la moquerie des gens satisfaits et du mépris des arrogants.
fr.R: Nous sommes fatigués que des gens à la vie facile se moquent de nous, et que des orgueilleux nous regardent de haut.

decisions.reason: The word (sha'anan) means untroubled and secure. Here it describes people comfortable enough to look down on others (Amos 6:1; Isaiah 32:9).
The verse takes up the end of verse 3, "much ... filled", and says what the contempt was and who showed it.
As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.
